(hereinafter referred to as "the DV Act") arises out of order dated 13.08.2019 passed by Ld.
MM Mahila Court-01 South-East in complaint case no. 630588/2016 titled as Seema and Another Vs. Om Prakash and Others.

entities.text: Seema and Another Vs. Om Prakash and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By way of the said order, the Ld. MM allowed an application moved by the Respondent herein and directed DNA Test upon the child of Appellant to ascertain paternity.
2. Along with the appeal, an application under Section 5 of The Limitation Act was also filed seeking condonation of delay in filing the appeal.
The impugned order was passed on 13.08.2019 whereas the appeal was filed on 25.01.2020.
The period of limitation of 30 days for preferring an appeal expired on 12.09.2019.
By way of the said application it was argued that the brother of the Appellant had suffered a fall from 3rd floor of a building and as a result he went in coma.
The entire family was under severe shock and depression and therefore could not approach the court with an appeal within time.
The CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash page 2 of 10 application was supported by a duly sworn affidavit in respect of the facts mentioned in the application.

entities.text: CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Section 5 of the Limitation Act grants discretion to a court to condone delay where the court is of the opinion that there existed sufficient cause which prevented a litigant from approaching the court within the prescribed time.

4. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Bharat Kalra Vs Raj Kumar Chhabra CM(M)-429/21 dated 12.08.2021 had opined as under:-
"While it is true that the power to condone delay is intended to advance substantive justice, nevertheless, procedure cannot be given a complete go by.

entities.text: Bharat Kalra Vs Raj Kumar Chhabra CM(M)-429/21 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The powers of the court to condone delay is to be used in appropriate cases.

No litigant can assume that,
as a matter of right, the delay in taking steps would be condoned, because procedure is hand maiden of substantive justice.
Rights accruing to the opposite party on ground of delayed action need to be also kept in mind.
The reasons given for explaining the delay are of paramount importance and not the length of delay.
The shortness of delay alone ought not to suffice for exercise of discretion to condone it.

Cogent and clear explanations have led the courts to condone the delay, even of 5 years in filing the pleadings".
5.

Coming to the facts of the present case, I am of the considered view that delay has been sufficiently explained and such delay should not be the only ground to prevent the Appellant from seeking her legal remedy.
Accordingly, the delay stands condoned.
The application is accordingly disposed off.
CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash page 3 of 10 6.

entities.text: CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Coming to the instant appeal, it has been argued by the Ld. Counsel for the Appellant that the application seeking paternity test was filed by the Respondent before the Ld. Trial Court only for the purpose of harassing the Appellant and to escape his responsibility to pay maintenance to the Appellant.

It was argued that a similar application was filed by the Respondent before Ld. Family Seema vs Sh. Om Prakash on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141809928/
2 Court which was also dismissed and the said order of dismissal was upheld by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court.

entities.text: Ld. Family Seema vs Sh. Om Prakash
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also sought to be argued that the Ld. MM failed to give any proper opportunity to the Appellant to prove the real date of birth of her child.
As such, it was prayed that the impugned order be set aside.
7. The appeal was contested on behalf of the Respondent.
It was argued by the Ld. Counsel for the Respondent that a well reasoned order has been passed by Ld. Trial Court.

It was further argued that the Ld. Trial Court duly considered the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court and at that time, the evidence of the Appellant in separate 498 A IPC proceedings were not available.

It was argued that the Appellant admitted during her cross-examination in case FIR no. 587/07 PS Kotla Mubarak Pur that she had left her matrimonial house on 30.03.2007 and that there was no access/meeting between her and her husband after 30.03.2017.
It was also argued that as per the school documents placed on record by the Appellant, the date of birth of the child was 31.03.2008.

As such it was argued that since the parties had no access to each other CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs.
Om Prakash page 4 of 10 after 30.03.2017, then the child born on 31.03.2008 could not have been from the same wedlock.

entities.text:
CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs.
Om Prakash
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Perusal of the impugned order dated 13.08.2019 would reveal that the Ld. MM discussed the order dated 16.12.2013 passed by Ld. Family Court whereby similar application seeking paternity test was declined and also the order dated 07.09.2016 passed by Hon'ble High Court in Criminal MC no. 1085/14 whereby the Hon'ble High Court upheld the order of the Ld. Family Court.

The Ld. MM vide its impugned order also considered the judgment dated 18.09.2018 passed in a separate proceedings arising out of FIR no. 587/07 PS Kotla Mubarak Pur whereby the Respondent no.1 herein was acquitted for the offence under Section 498A/406/34 IPC.
9.

The Ld. MM came to a conclusion that after passing of judgment in case FIR no. 587/07 PS Kotla Mubarak Pur, there is sufficient evidence to rebut the presumption of Section 112 of the Evidence Act and therefore paternity test is required to be conducted upon the child.
10. Section 112 of the Evidence Act is reproduced herein for convenience:
"112. Birth during marriage, conclusive proof of legitimacy- the fact that any person was born during the continuance of valid marriage between his mother or any man,
or within 280 days (two CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash page 5 of 10 hundred eighty days) after its dissolution, the mother remaining unmarried, shall be conclusive proof that he is the son of that man, unless it can be shown that the parties to the marriage had no access to each other at any time when he could have been begotten."
11.
It is well settled that the presumption of legitimacy is a presumption of law.
When a child is born from a wedlock, there is a presumption in favour of his legitimacy.

The rule of evidence contained in Section 112 of the Evidence Act raises a mandatory presumption that a child born during wedlock,
no matter when the child could be begotten is the legitimate issue of the husband of the mother.

Seema vs Sh. Om Prakash on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141809928/
3 12.

In Lal Hari Bansha Vs. Nikunj Behari Ilr 1960 Cuttack 230 the Hon'ble High Court reiterated the relevant principle of law as under:-
" Odiosa Et Inkonesta Non Sunt In Lege Praa Sunenda"
which means 'nothing odius or dishonourable will be presumed by law'.

entities.text: Lal Hari Bansha Vs. Nikunj Behari Ilr 1960 Cuttack 230
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So the law presumes against vice and immorality.
One of the strongest illustrations of the principle is the presumption in favour of legitimacy of children in a civilised society.

entities.text: Goutam Kundu Vs. State of West Bengal and Anr AIR 1993 SC 2295
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) There must be a strong prima-facie case in that the husband must establish non-access in order to dispell the presumption arising under Section 112 of the Evidence Act.

(iv) The court must carefully examine as to what would be the consequence of ordering the blood test ; whether it will have the effect of branding a child as a bastard and the mother as an unchaste women.
(v) No one can be compelled to give sample of blood for analysis."

14. Further in Bhabani Prasad Jena Vs. Convinor Secretary, Odisha State Commission for Women AIR 2010 SC 285, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that DNA test is a matter relating to paternity of a child and it should not be directed by the court as a matter of course or in a routine manner,
whenever such a request is made, the court has to consider diverse aspects including presumption u/s 112 of the Act, pros and cons of such order and the test of "eminent need" whether it is not possible for the court to reach the truth without use of such test.

entities.text: Bhabani Prasad Jena Vs. Convinor Secretary, Odisha State Commission for Women AIR 2010 SC 285
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The result of a genuine DNA test may not be enough to escape from the conclusiveness of Section 112 of the Act.
CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash page 7 of 10 15.

entities.text: CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The law as enunciated in the aforecited decisions is abundantly clear that once the validity of marriage is proved then there is strong presumption about the legitimacy of child born out of that wedlock.
The presumption can only be rebutted by a strong, clear, satisfying and conclusive evidence.
The presumption cannot be displaced by mere balance of probabilities or any circumstance creating doubt.

4
16. Coming to the facts of the present case, admittedly the marriage between the Appellant and the Respondent was solemnised on 13.12.2006.
There is no doubt that it was a valid marriage.
As per the appellant's case, she was thrown out of her matrimonial house on 30.03.2007.
The marriage still subsists.
The child was born during continuance of the marriage and hence presumption u/s 112 of the Evidence Act stood drawn in the present case.

17. The Respondents allege that during her evidence recorded as PW-1 in case FIR no. 587/07 PS Kotla Mubarak Pur, the appellant had given inconsistent answers as to whether she was allowed to stay in the same room as her husband or whether she had any access to him in the matrimonial house at all.

It was also pointed out on behalf of the Respondents that the Appellant also admitted during her cross- examination that she had left the matrimonial house on 30.03.2007 and she has had no access to her husband after 30.03.2007.

It was also pointed out that as per the school record,
the date of birth of the child is CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash page 8 of 10 31.03.2008.

entities.text: CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was argued that since as per her own admission, the Appellant and the Respondent no.1 did not have any access between them for a period of 1 year immediately preceding the birth of the child,
then it cannot be said that the child was fathered by Respondent no. 1.
This argument of Ld. Counsel for the Respondent cannot be accepted.

A perusal of the said cross-examination of Appellant as PW-1 in case FIR no. 587/07 PS Kotla Mubarak Pur would show that she did not accept the date of birth of the child to be 31.03.2008 rather she claimed that it was 31.12.2007.
Ld. Counsel for the Respondent seeks to cherry-pick the testimony of Appellant in a separate proceedings which cannot be allowed.

Further the testimony of the Appellant in such separate proceedings, where it was not proved that the child was not born out of the wedlock or was born on 31.03.2008, the same cannot be deemed to be conclusive evidence sufficient to dislodge the presumption u/s 112 of the Evidence Act.
18. The Evidence in present proceedings before the Ld. Trial Cout is yet to be recorded.
Onus is upon the Respondent to prove during Trial by producing such evidence that he did not have any access to the Appellant.
Further, for the purpose of Section 112, "access" does not mean actual marital intercourse; opportunity of intercourse is enough.
Further, Appellant also needs to be aforded an opportunity to bring documents or material on record by way of evidence to show on which date the child was born.
Such claims and counter claims need to be CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash page 9 of 10 tested on the touchstone of cross-examination.

entities.text: CA No. 39/2020 Seema Vs. Om Prakash
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. The Ld. MM in the instant case erred by pre-judging the issue.

Ld. MM was not correct in basing her opinion merely on the testimony of Appellant in separate proceedings where the issue of date of birth of the child and access between parties was not conclusively decided.
20. Accordingly, the impugned order dated 13.08.2019 as well as the consequent proceedings are set aside.
Ld. MM is directed to proceed with the matter as per law.
With the said observation, the present appeal stands disposed off as allowed.
